perspective:
Gloria Bangura has access to the following:

- She is Gloria Bangura, an administrative assistant at a large event planning company, where Donald Ortega works as a part-time bartender during events.
- She and Donald are colleagues but not personally close; they mostly interact during company events.
- Over several events, she directly observed Donald’s distracted demeanor and lack of enthusiasm while serving drinks.
- She approached Donald and asked if everything was okay with his job.
- Donald told her he was “not as into it as I used to be” and that the work felt “repetitive.”
- After reflecting on their conversation, she suspected his job dissatisfaction might point to larger personal issues.
- She suggested Donald consider talking to a professional.
- Donald told her he hadn’t considered that and wasn’t sure it would help.
- After that conversation, she sensed a change in Donald’s behavior toward her and worried he might resent her suggestion as overstepping.
- She apologized to Donald, explaining she only wanted to help because she cared.
- Donald told her he had been “a bit taken aback at first” but knew she meant well, and said it was “a lot to process.”
- She felt the apology had eased the tension and wanted to strengthen their working relationship.
- She invited Donald to collaborate on an upcoming project, saying it could use his creative input.
- Donald accepted, thanked her, and said he wanted to be more involved.
- After the collaboration, she observed Donald’s significant contributions and renewed enthusiasm.
- She publicly acknowledged Donald’s work during a team meeting, praising his contributions as crucial to the project’s success.
- Donald thanked her, saying it meant a lot, that he was glad to contribute, and that it felt great to be appreciated.
